labelling: SIMULATED — all states, timestamps, people, sellers and amounts in this file are seeded demo data. No real payment, courier or provider system is connected.
title: Hero scenario: 4 items, 3 sellers, split payment, two returns, a pickup fight, an inspection dispute and a three-source status mismatch

order.shippingNote: Free shipping: payable 200000 paise is above the 99900 paise (₹999) free-shipping threshold at checkout. After both returns the kept items total 66667 paise, below the threshold — the threshold effect is previewed as a policy line before return confirmation (conflict C-05); this demo applies the goodwill policy and does not claw the shipping benefit back from the refunds.

payments.note: Normal-speed card refund budget: 5-7 working days.
Wallet refund budget: ~2 hours after approval.
Voucher money refunds as a voucher, never to bank.

customer.name: A. Sharma
customer.returnsNote: This is the seeded heavy returner of conflict C-12: 12 returns in 90 days, all sizing/fit on apparel and footwear, all legitimate. The fraud ladder may add friction up to level 2 and must not escalate beyond it; an appeal is on file and a human reviewer overturned the escalation (see heavy-returners.json HR-1).

allocationMatrix.method: pro-rata: coupon allocated by list-price share (largest remainder); each item effective price split across instruments by payment shares 60/25/15 (largest remainder per row); rows and columns verified to sum exactly

returns.idempotencyNote: One stable refund-intent id for this return. Retries, double-taps and duplicate webhooks reuse RI-R1-0001 and can never mint a second refund (conflicts C-02, C-03).

pickupAttempts.bundleCompleteness: thin — timestamp, GPS and call log present, but no doorstep photo; the courier claim is automatically downgraded and cannot be taken at face value (conflict C-07)
full — timestamp, GPS, call log and doorstep photo all present (conflict C-07)

returns.claimNote: Courier evidence bundles and the customer claim disagree. Neither side is auto-believed: the case sits in the conflicting-claims state, a reschedule plus a drop-off fallback were offered, and the third attempt succeeded.

checklist: No visible wear on upper or sole
doorstepQcSnapshot.note: This snapshot is frozen at handover and shared with the customer. The warehouse cannot silently overwrite it — a different warehouse verdict becomes a visible dispute (conflict C-08).

warehouseInspection.inspectorNote: Sole shows wear consistent with outdoor use.

inspectionDispute.basis: Frozen doorstep QC snapshot says pass (photos EV-01, EV-03, 5-point checklist); warehouse verdict says used. Photo proof is mandatory for any deduction.
inspectionDispute.conditionTierProposed: used — deduction up to 50% if the warehouse verdict is upheld after human review
inspectionDispute.proposedPartialNote: 50% of the item effective price 88889 paise, floored to 44444 paise, payable only if a human reviewer upholds the warehouse verdict with photo proof (conflict C-15). Until the dispute resolves, the legs below stay at the full matrix-row amounts and no deduction is applied silently.
inspectionDispute.slaNote: Human review SLA 48 hours from dispute opening; the customer sees the doorstep snapshot and the warehouse photos side by side.

legs.classificationReason: Lifecycle mismatch (planted conflict C-01): the provider reports a terminal state, reversed, while the seller record still says pending. A terminal-state contradiction is stuck regardless of age; the reconciler raises a break, owns it, and customer copy must not claim the money has arrived.

provider.reference: ARN-764301198822 (refund later reversed by the issuing bank)

legs.classificationReason: All three sources agree the wallet leg is credited. Wallet budget is ~2 hours after approval; the credit landed inside it.

All three sources agree on pending and the leg is inside its latency budget, so this is waiting, not stuck. Planted pressure (conflict C-04): the re-issued voucher keeps the original expiry, which is close — the customer must be told the expiry date in the refund preview, not discover it later.

voucherReissue.note: Re-issued voucher carries the original expiry of 2026-11-02, 9 days after the refund was initiated.

legs.classificationReason: Card refunds run 5-7 working days at normal speed; at 24 hours this leg is well inside its budget. Split refunds arriving on different days is normal and is shown per leg.
Inside the ~2 hour wallet budget; provider confirmation is the only outstanding step.
Voucher re-issue is near-instant once approved; at 1 hour the leg is inside budget. Refunds as a voucher, never to bank.

timeline.detail: Order HERO-1 placed: 4 items, 3 sellers, list total 225000 paise, coupon SAVE250 of 25000 paise, payable 200000 paise.
Item x instrument allocation matrix computed at checkout (pro-rata coupon, largest remainder) and persisted. All later refunds read this matrix; nothing is re-derived.
All 4 items delivered in one shipment.
Returns requested for ITEM-1 (shoes) and ITEM-2 (t-shirt), both sizing. Per-item eligibility and refund previews shown before confirmation, including the free-shipping threshold policy line.
Refund intents RI-R1-0001 and RI-R2-0001 minted once. These ids are the idempotency keys for every downstream call.
R-1 attempt 1 failed: customer_unreachable. Evidence bundle has timestamp, GPS and call log but NO doorstep photo — bundle scored thin, courier claim downgraded.
R-2 handed over at the doorstep on attempt 1 with a full evidence bundle; doorstep QC snapshot frozen (pass) and shared with the customer.
R-1 attempt 2 failed: customer_unreachable, this time with a full evidence bundle including a doorstep photo.
Customer states "I was home both times". R-1 enters the conflicting-claims state; reschedule and a drop-off fallback are offered. Neither side is auto-believed.
R-2 warehouse inspection: pass, consistent with its doorstep snapshot. Refund legs proceed on their own clocks.
R-1 wallet leg of 22222 paise credited — all three sources agree.

R-1 card leg reported reversed by the provider while the seller record still says pending — planted mismatch C-01. Reconciler classifies the leg stuck (terminal-state contradiction) and raises a break.
R-1 handed over on the rescheduled attempt 3; doorstep QC snapshot frozen with verdict pass (photos EV-01, EV-03) and shared with the customer at 09:13.
R-1 warehouse inspection verdict: used — contradicting the frozen doorstep pass snapshot (conflict C-08).

Dispute DSP-R1-1 opened. Any deduction needs human review with photo proof; the proposed ceiling is the used tier (up to 50%, conflict C-15). Legs stay at full matrix amounts until the dispute resolves.

Demo state: R-2 legs waiting inside their budgets; R-1 wallet settled, voucher waiting inside budget (near-expiry expiry 2026-11-02 surfaced), card leg stuck on the provider/seller mismatch; inspection dispute open. A judge pressing "retry refund" now hits the idempotency guard on RI-R1-0001 and no second refund is issued.
